queries.query: Before we act on it, adversarially fact-check this draft research recommendation against sources and our code. Draft: "We should adopt hyparquet for our analytics export because (1) its bloom filter reader lets us skip row groups on equality filters, (2) parquetQuery stops reading row groups once rowEnd matches are found, (3) asyncBufferFromUrl streams with Range requests so memory stays bounded, and (4) it decodes geospatial columns to GeoJSON." Give each claim a verdict with evidence.

Verify our draft performance note before it goes out. It claims: parquetMetadataAsync reads the footer in one request; cachedAsyncBuffer removes duplicate range reads; the planner in src/plan.js merges nearby column chunks into fewer fetches; and the bloom filter check runs before any page is decoded. Check each claim against src/ and the Parquet spec, and mark what is unsupported.

Review-only pass on this research summary, no code changes. The summary says hyparquet supports every Parquet encoding the spec lists, decodes DELTA_BINARY_PACKED, DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY and DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY in src/delta.js, handles BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT, and decompresses only snappy without extra codecs. Try to refute each point against the code and cite the lines.

We are about to recommend this reader to another team. Fact-check our recommendation memo first: it says the reader runs in the browser and in Node with no dependencies, rejects bad rowStart and unknown orderBy arguments in parquetQuery, throws on corrupt snappy input, and keeps memory flat for large files read over HTTP. Tier each claim and show the evidence.

A consultant sent us this assessment of the reader and we plan to act on it next sprint: the footer parser trusts the metadata length without bounds checks, the snappy decoder can loop forever on crafted input, and the bloom filter code ignores the hash seed the spec requires. Which of these hold up in src/, and which are wrong?

Our migration plan rests on three assumptions about this codebase: parquetRead returns rows in file order even when row groups are fetched out of order, convert.js turns INT96 timestamps into Date objects, and the column index lets the reader skip pages inside a row group. Before we commit, tell me which assumptions are safe and which would bite us, with evidence.

Here is the paragraph from our architecture doc about this reader: "Reads are lazy. The file is never loaded whole, each column chunk is fetched once, and decoding happens page by page so peak memory tracks one page per column." I do not trust it. Go through src/ and tell me what is accurate, what is overstated, and what is simply false.

Someone wrote a comparison claiming this reader beats the alternatives because it pushes filters down to row groups using statistics, uses bloom filters when statistics cannot decide, and never decodes a column the query does not select. Poke holes in each part of that claim using the code in src/query.js, src/plan.js and src/bloom.js before we cite it.
A teammate says parquetMetadataAsync always reads the whole footer in a single 512kb request. Prove or disprove that against src/metadata.js.
I am about to tell the team that snappyUncompress throws on corrupt input instead of returning garbage. Am I right? Show me where in src/snappy.js.
We want to add a row-group cache to src/read.js. Write a code-grounded design brief for it before anyone builds it.
Should we replace the vendored decoder in src/snappy.js with a maintained package, or keep it? Give a verdict with migration cost.
What changed lately in the parquet-format spec and in other Parquet readers that needs action in this code: new codecs, encodings, deprecations?
Give me novel feature ideas for this Parquet reader, grounded in src/ and current trends in columnar data tooling.
Suggest improvements to the predicate pushdown in src/filter.js and src/plan.js based on outside best practice for row-group skipping.
Run the whole research pipeline end to end on how this reader should support ZSTD and GZIP, with me in the loop.
Hunt for defects in src/delta.js and src/plan.js, and rank what you find by severity with a reproduction for each.
Pull the current Parquet format documentation for the page index and bloom filter structures before I touch src/indexes.js.
What does the Array.prototype.flatMap method do in JavaScript? Answer in two sentences.
Say hello and tell me which date format ISO 8601 uses.
